item.title: Family and Party Solidarity on Display at PDI-P Gathering
item.description: Jakarta. Megawati Soekarnoputri, chairwoman of the Indonesian Democratic Party of Struggle (PDI-P), shared a rare public moment of family warmth with her two children during the party’s National Working Meeting in Jakarta on Sunday. Megawati was embraced and kissed simultaneously by her son, Prananda Prabowo, and her daughter, Puan Maharani, symbolizing both family closeness and internal party unity. item.description: Jakarta. President Prabowo Subianto on Sunday convened an unscheduled meeting with several cabinet ministers at his private residence to discuss a range of strategic issues, including the development of Indonesia’s semiconductor industry. item.title: Touches 9,000 in Early Trade, JCI Extends Record Rally
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s benchmark stock index briefly crossed the 9,000 threshold mark at Monday’s open, extending its record run as early buying pushed the Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) briefly through the psychological level. JCI opened 0.61% higher, up 55 points at 8,991, after touching 9,000 in the first minutes of trading. The index moved within a tight range of 8,957–9,000. item.title: Amy Poehler's Podcast, 'Kpop Demon Hunters' Win At Golden Globes
item.description: At the 83rd Golden Globes, Amy Poehler won the inaugural award for podcasting, “KPop Demons Hunters” triumphed in the best song category, and Seth Rogen won a comically poignant award for his Hollywood satire “The Studio.” For the first year, the Globes handed out a best podcast trophy. item.title: Indonesia’s 30,000-Ton Meat Import Quota Too Small For Private Sector
item.description: Jakarta. Businesses are unhappy with Indonesia’s decision to slash the meat import quota for private companies to just 30,000 tons this year. Indonesia is planning to import around 297,000 tons of meat throughout 2026. The country will allocate 250,000 tons of that quota to state-run enterprises, namely: Berdikari and Perusahaan Perdagangan Indonesia (PPI). item.title: Antam Gold Breaks Rp 2.63 Million Record as Global Safe-Haven Rush Lifts Prices
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s retail gold market opened 2026 with a bang as Antam bullion prices surged to a fresh all-time high on Monday, tracking a global rally fueled by safe-haven demand amid rising geopolitical tensions. Data from Aneka Tambang’s Logam Mulia website showed Antam gold jumping Rp 29,000 to Rp 2,631,000 ($156.09) per gram, eclipsing the previous record of Rp 2,605,000 set on Dec. 27, 2025.
